title: Private Access certificate trust: tenant CAs, Zscaler PKI, pinning and key custody

prose.text: Private Access authenticates both ends of every connection with certificates from two different authorities. [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:pki-roles]]

prose.label: Who accepts whom.
prose.text: {{mutual-acceptance}} The same rule for App Connectors: [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment:cert-signed-by-tenant-ca]]. [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:no-mitm-pinning]] [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:identity-key-only]]

prose.label: Expiry and clocks.
prose.text: How long a connector certificate lasts and how it renews is open: [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment:certificate-validity-window]]. A wrong connector clock delays enrollment: [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment:clock-skew-delays-cert]]. An SSL-intercepting device in the path breaks the pinned connection: [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:ssl-interception-unsupported]].

checks.do: When a connector or client cannot connect, check certificate trust (interception device, clock, enrollment) before access policy.

mutual-acceptance.statement: Private Access accepts Zscaler Client Connector connections only with a client certificate signed by a CA associated with the tenant, and Client Connector and App Connector connect only to Private Access components that present a certificate signed by the Private Access infrastructure PKI.

quotes: Private Access only accepts connections from Zscaler Client Connector and the App Connector instances that present a client certificate signed by a CA associated with each tenant.
Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector will only connect to Private Access service components that present a certificate signed by the Private Access infrastructure PKI.

tenant-ca-keys-encrypted.statement: The private keys for each organization's CA, which the article expands as Central Authority, are stored in encrypted format (AES256-GCM).

quotes: The private keys for each organization's Central Authority (CA) are stored in encrypted format (i.e., AES256-GCM).

tenant-ca-keys-encrypted.conditions: The article expands CA here as Central Authority, although the surrounding paragraph is about certificates signed by each organization's CA.

per-tenant-isolation.statement: Because client certificates are verified against a CA associated with the tenant, a Client Connector or App Connector certificate issued for one tenant is not expected to authenticate to another tenant's Private Access.
per-tenant-isolation.conditions: Inference from the per-tenant signing scope; no source states the cross-tenant case.

chain-before-policy.statement: A connection whose certificate does not verify is rejected before any request crosses it, so such a failure points to the certificate chain, an interception device or the clock rather than to access policy.
chain-before-policy.conditions: Inference: all component traffic runs inside the mutually verified TLS connection, so policy cannot be reached without it. No source describes the failure sequence.
